findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a staff member wash their hands, then fail to use a barrier to turn off the faucet. CORRECTED- education was provided. Ensure the use of a barrier after completing hand washing to prevent re-contaminating hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed ground beef at 119F. CORRECTED- it was verified that the food had been in the unit less than 4 hours, and the unit was turned from “1” to “3”. Food was then observed to have an internal temperature of 140F. Ensure hot holding units are always set so that hot temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods have an internal temperature of 135F or higher.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed TCS foods in the standing cooler (nearest the door) to have internal temperatures between 45-50 (hotdogs and hamburgers respectively). CORRECTED- items that had been in the unit less than 4 hours were moved to a working cooler or implemented under time as control (items are to be used or discarded within 4 hours). Items housed in the unit over 4 hours were discarded. Ensure all TCS foods (including all animal proteins, house made products using mayo as an ingredient, cut tomatoes, and shredded lettuce) are cold held at or below 41F, or above 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the standing cooler nearest to door to have an ambient temperature of 50F, and failing to hold TCS items at or below 41F (see violation #22). A follow up is being scheduled for 6/26/26 to verify compliance. Ensure the unit has been serviced to cold hold foods below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: The Certified Food Protection Manager (CFM/CFPM) on staff does not have Allergen Awareness training. Inspector provided Allergen Awareness training information to the PIC. Ensure all CFMs obtain Allergen Awareness training, to be maintained on file every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The person in charge (PIC) was unable to produce their Certified Food Manager (CFM/ CFPM) certificate during today’s inspection. CORRECTED- a CFM arrived on site. Ensure a CFM is present on site at all times food is being cooked or prepared, and maintain files on site for future inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket in the kitchen to contain soap, and no measurable concentration of sanitizer. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bucket was remade to display 200 ppm Cl. Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are made with ONLY warm water and a chemical sanitizer, as soap interferes with sanitizing ability of chemical.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an unlabeled white powder in the kitchen. CORRECTED- a kitchen staff member labeled the product as sugar. Ensure any ready to eat (RTE) food products that may be easily mistaken for another is labeled once removed from its original container to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Multiple nonfood contact surfaces where observed to be in need of repair or reconditioning:
1) The gaskets at BOTH standing coolers and the standing freezer in the kitchen are fragmenting.
2) One of the microwave handles is loose from the door.
3) Some shelves in the standing cooler directly next to the fryers are rusted. Clean/ reseal/ paint, or replace rusting shelves.
Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are in proper repair to prevent potential contamination of foods. Nonfoodcontact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable.
 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.[C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
The only Allergen certificates available were observed to have been expired. Inspector provided Allergen Awareness training information to the PIC. Ensure CFMs obtain Allergen Awareness training, to be maintained every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee washing their hands. Upon completion of hand washing, the employee turned off the faucet with a bare hand. Inspector talked with the employee, as well as the PIC about hand washing procedures. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after washing hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a build-up of soils on the soda nozzles of the soda machine. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that soda nozzles are cleaned regularly enough to keep soils from depositing. Inspector will return 07/28/2025 to re-inspect the condition of the soda nozzles.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the facility to not have any quat test strips. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the proper test strips are kept in the facility at all times. Inspector will return 07/28/2025 to check and see if test strips have been acquired.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no date marks on juices being used in bar coolers. Discussed date marking procedures with PIC. PIC added date marks to the open juices in the cooler. Ensure all opened TCS foods are date-marked upon opening.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Ice machine contained mold and mildew on baffles.  Discussed with PIC, corrected on site.  Ensure ice machine is cleaned regularly to prevent contamination of ice.

4-602.11: (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.
